_README: Hand judgement of all 16 citation-support flags from the two laser curricula
re-run in `guardrails-v1` Item 3, after the claim-unit fix landed. Not a
sample: 16 is the whole population of flags from those two runs (9/120 and
7/118 = 16/238 = 6.7%), so there is no sampling question.
Companion to dl_flag_verdicts.json, which judged all 37 flags from the
2026-08-31 pair. Regenerate the evidence with
python scripts/classify_dl_flags.py --runs C D
Row order is the order the flags appear in evidence_mapping.jsonl.
THE VERDICT SET HAS CHANGED, and the changes are the finding.
artifact_tail  is GONE as a category. The judge is shown the whole
abstract now, so a supporting sentence cannot sit past a
cut. It was 17 of the previous 37.
artifact_unit  has nearly gone: 13 of the previous 37, 2 of these 16, and
both survivors are one list item carrying TWO assertions
about two different papers rather than a whole decision
tree carrying seven.
artifact_negative is NEW, and it is now the largest class: 7 of 16. The
claim is of the form 'X et al. did not report <parameter>'
or 'no adverse events were reported in the reviewed RCTs'.
The claim is TRUE and the marker names the right paper.
It cannot be verified from an abstract, because an abstract
cannot state what it omits. `_GROUNDING_RULE` explicitly
asks for this move -- 'take the number from the paper that
reports it, OR state that the cited study did not report
it' -- so the rule and the checker disagree about whether a
negative carries a marker. That is a prompt question, and
it is the same SHAPE of collision Item 2 resolved for the
recommendation.
artifact_meta  is also new, 2 of 16: the claim is about the EVIDENCE BASE
('the evidence base does not specify a minimum canal
diameter'), not about the cited paper, and carries a marker
anyway.
unsupported    5 of 16 = 2.1% of the 238 checked pairs, against 3.0%
(7/234) on the previous pair. Two are a mechanism claim
cited to a review that reports outcomes, one is a bare
procedural directive, one cites an SR's finding to an RCT,
and one -- the best catch in the set -- justifies a
recommendation for SMALL lesions (PAI <= 2) with a trial
that enrolled PAI >= 3. Every one of those is a trap
`_GROUNDING_RULE` names by name.

verdicts.why: A MECHANISM claim -- diode wavelengths absorbed by chromophores in pigmented bacteria and soft tissue rather than water or enamel -- cited to a 1,896-character narrative review of laser APPLICATIONS. The review lists device types and says it discusses 'different wavelengths'; it does not state the absorption target. Grounding-rule trap 1, verbatim.

'Irrigate with 5.25% NaOCl after each file sequence' is a bare procedural directive carrying a marker to an in vitro dye-penetration and microhardness study of PIPS/SWEEPS. The paper's protocol is not this protocol, and a step instruction is not a finding of any paper.

'No serious adverse events were reported in the RCTs reviewed by Meire et al.' The word adverse, harm and safety appear nowhere in the 3,015-character abstract -- checked. The claim is an argument from silence, which is TRUE of the abstract and unverifiable from it.
'the evidence base does not specify a minimum canal diameter' is a claim about the evidence base as a whole, attached to one umbrella review. No single paper can support or refute it.
'Erkan et al. did not report exact exposure duration per cycle.' Correct paper, correct statement, unverifiable shape.
'Das et al. did not standardize photosensitizer concentration or irradiation time across included studies.' Same shape.
'the evidence base for adjunctive laser disinfection is concentrated in this diagnosis' -- again a statement about the corpus, marked to one member of it.

One list item, two assertions, two papers. The half carrying THIS marker -- single-visit RoCT shows higher one-week pain, RR 1.55 (95% CI 1.14-2.09), moderate certainty -- is VERBATIM in this Cochrane abstract, checked. The half that is not supported belongs to Meire et al., whose marker is flag 9. The list-item rule did not split a semicolon.
The other marker on the same compound list item as flag 8.

Diode absorption by haemoglobin and melanin, cited to a 1,520-character narrative review whose subject is cavitation in laser-ACTIVATED IRRIGATION. Neither chromophore is in it. Grounding-rule trap 1 again, and the same wavelength-mechanism sentence as flag 1 -- the module writes this claim and reaches for whichever laser review is nearest.
'Fahim et al. did not report a specific final apical instrument size.'
'Wang et al. did not report a specific cycle duration for Er,Cr:YSGG.'
'Fahim et al. did not specify final rinse volume.' Third of three in one module, all the same shape, all the same instruction being followed.

A 2025 PROSPERO-registered systematic review of aPDT -- 11 studies, meta-analysis of 5 -- cited to a single-centre RCT of an 810 nm semiconductor laser in 202 patients. The marker names a paper of the wrong design for the claim it carries.

Two halves: the Cochrane review's LLLT finding, which it does state, and 'reported no thermal or soft-tissue adverse events in included RCTs', which is again an argument from silence. The unverifiable half is what carries the flag.

THE BEST CATCH IN THE SET, and it is on a decision-tree branch that the old splitter would have buried in a seven-branch blob. The branch recommends LAI for a SMALL periapical lesion, PAI <= 2, and justifies it with this trial -- which enrolled 'periapical lesions ... and a periapical index score of 3 or higher' and is titled for LARGE lesions. Checked in the abstract. A recommendation generalised past the cited paper's population is grounding-rule trap 4, and un-merging the tree is what made it visible.
